item.title: EUROPA: The Greek mythological origin of Europe's name
item.description: The name "Europe" is derived from the Greek mythological figure Europa, a Phoenician princess who was abducted by Zeus in the form of a bull. According to the myth, Zeus was enamored with Europa's beauty and transformed himself into a white bull to seduce her. The name "Europa" is believed to come from the Greek words "eurus" (wide) and "ops" (face), symbolizing a "wide-eyed" or "broad-faced" person, which may refer to the full moon or the vastness of the continent.
